title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element

constraints.impact: O(n²) is about 10¹⁰ steps: far too slow. Sorting, O(n log n), plus one O(n) pass is fine. The answer is always at least 1.

constraints.meaning: Every value is positive and at most 100,000.
constraints.impact: A window sum can reach 10⁵ × 10⁵ = 10¹⁰, which does not fit in int. Use long long for total and cost in C and C++.

constraints.meaning: At most k increments in total, spread over any elements.
constraints.impact: k is a budget for the whole window, not per element. A window is valid while the increments it needs are at most k.

constraints.meaning: Values can only go up, never down.
constraints.impact: Values can only be raised to a bigger value, so the target of a group is its largest value. After sorting, the cheapest values to raise to nums[right] are the ones just before it: a contiguous window.

bruteForce.summary: sort nums, then for each right try every left from right down to 0, adding up the increments needed to raise nums[left..right] to nums[right]. Stop when the cost goes over k. O(n²) time, which is too slow for n = 10⁵.
